fields.description:
## Symptom

An operator's local status change is silently reverted by the Jira reconciler, minutes later,
with every OTHER field write from the same period left intact. Confirmed twice on 2026-08-07:

- `858c-786a-13be-4332` (REB-2500): reopened `closed -> open` at 10:09:14Z; reconciler wrote
  `open -> closed` at 10:17:58Z. The description rewrite from the same window SURVIVED.
- `556a-5a1f-adb3-4139` (REB-1504): moved `in_progress -> open` at 10:09:02Z; reconciler wrote
  `open -> in_progress` at 10:17:52Z.

Both events are authored `reconciler` / `env_id: reconciler`, e.g.
`.tickets-tracker/858c-786a-13be-4332/1786097878273766164-d80fab3f-...-STATUS.json`:
`{"author":"reconciler","env_id":"reconciler","data":{"current_status":"open","status":"closed"}}`.

The projection/reducer is NOT at fault: the reconciler event is genuinely the LATEST status
event in the log. This is an inbound write, not a replay defect.

## Proven root cause — the baseline lags our own outbound push by exactly one pass

ADR 0026 Decision 1 makes the per-binding baseline the sole direction signal:
`local == baseline` is taken to mean "local did not change, so a differing remote must be a
Jira-side edit — stand down and let inbound mirror it"
(`outbound_field_diff.py:323-334` `_suppressed_by_inbound`, applied to status at `:389-396`).
Inbound has no arbitration of its own — it is pure value inequality
(`inbound_differ.py:233-234`), and it only ever clobbers a field in a pass where outbound
emitted nothing for that field (same-pass suppression, `inbound_differ.py:709-718`).

The baseline is advanced from the pass-START snapshot (`reconcile.py:595` calling
`_advance_baselines`, `reconcile.py:514-531`, with `ctx.curr_snapshot` fetched at
`reconcile.py:280` BEFORE the outbound apply). So in the pass where rebar itself pushes a status
to Jira, the baseline is left holding the OLD value.

That makes the guard's premise false for one pass. A REOPEN is a revert to a previous value, so:

1. Pass N (run 31168795002): local `closed`/`in_progress` pushed outbound —
   `RECON: outbound_update key=REB-2500 changed=[description,status]` and
   `key=REB-1504 changed=[...,status]`. Jira now holds `Done` / `In Progress`.
   Baseline NOT advanced: `.bridge_state/bindings.json` at f0fe2ce9d4 (10:14:45Z) still records
   `baseline.status = 'To Do'` for BOTH bindings.
2. Operator reopens locally to `open` (10:09).
3. Pass N+1 (run 31169292024): local `open` == canonicalized baseline `To Do` -> `open`, so
   `_suppressed_by_inbound` fires and status is omitted from outbound —
   `RECON: outbound_update key=REB-2500 changed=[description]`, `key=REB-1504 changed=[]`.
   Inbound then reads Jira's `Done`/`In Progress` and overwrites local. Clobber.

This is the same omit-vs-clear asymmetry class recorded on `39c1-2a32-b564-4b4b` for the
2026-08-03 parent-clear incident (`ed5e-f176-3aea-41fd`).

### Runtime reproduction (the discriminating experiment)

Replaying the real pass-time inputs through `outbound_field_diff.compute_update_fields`, with the
baseline as the ONLY variable:

    STALE baseline 'To Do' (the real pass-time value)
       -> outbound fields = {'description': 'NEW'}                     status_sent=False
    ADVANCED baseline 'Done' (what outbound had just pushed)
       -> outbound fields = {'description': 'NEW', 'status': 'To Do'}  status_sent=True

The stale-baseline row reproduces the observed `changed=[description]` exactly, including the
operator's discriminating detail: the description was NOT equal to the baseline so it WAS sent,
while status was suppressed. One variable flips the outcome.

## Why the description survived but the status did not

Not a revision rollback. Description differed from the (stale) baseline, so it was pushed
outbound and inbound had nothing to say. Status EQUALLED the stale baseline, so outbound stood
down and inbound won. The asymmetry is a direct consequence of the guard, not of event ordering.

## NOT a regression from 2026-08-07 changes

The clobbering pass is run 31169292024, started 10:14:54Z. Every suspect commit landed AFTER it:
e7a9 `33d6d4ef7c` 12:16:01Z, 851e `17c31cf5c8` 12:25:19Z, 2876 `c390cef54a` 12:34:40Z,
65d7 `08dfbbc689` 13:13:44Z. None was in the deployed tree.

Independently: a tracker-wide sweep for `author: reconciler` STATUS events finds the SAME shape
on 2026-07-20 15:21:03Z across 8 tickets (`0662-2b88-6fe3-4844`, `1416-b1bc-c8e9-477e`,
`542e-fb17-6f5d-4ced`, `caed-6c07-2a14-4ef9`, `7cab-bb99-9803-4ccb`, `9f60-2767-9ca3-45b2`,
`c03f-254f-014b-4cc7` open->closed, `6dac-d0d9-1a60-4998` in_progress->closed) — 18 days earlier.
Pre-existing defect, exposed today because the Reconcile Bridge was re-enabled mid-session.

## Blast radius

Any local status change made in the window between rebar's own outbound push of a status and the
next pass's baseline advance, where the new local value equals the pre-push baseline. Reopen and
un-claim are exactly that shape, so operator corrections are the most exposed operation. Silent:
the pass exits 0 and nothing is logged as a conflict.

## Approach (operator decision: OPTION A)

Restore ADR 0026's own definition of the baseline as the **last-SYNCED** value rather than the
last-FETCHED one, by overlaying the values rebar itself just pushed onto the pass-start snapshot
before `set_baseline` records it. Applied to all five `_INBOUND_MIRRORED_FIELDS`
(summary/description/priority/status/assignee), because all five share the
`_suppressed_by_inbound` guard and therefore share the ABA exposure.

**Per-mutation success is the gate, not the pass exit code.** The applier does not currently
expose a per-mutation outcome the baseline advance can key off, so that plumbing is part of this
change:

1. `dispatch_one._update_one_scalar_update` currently returns only the update result, which is
   `None` both when the call is skipped (parent-only mutation) and when the 400
   illegal-transition comment-fallback soft-fails. It will instead return
   `(result, fields_synced)` where `fields_synced` is the exact kwargs dict handed to
   `client.update_issue` **only when that call returned without raising**, and `{}` on the
   skip and soft-fail arms. This is deliberately conservative: any raise (including the
   `RuntimeError` from `acli.transition_issue_by_name` for an unreachable transition, the raw
   404, `AssigneeNotFoundError`, and any partial application inside `update_issue`) records
   NOTHING, so the baseline can only ever lag — never falsely lead.
2. `dispatch_one.update_one` gains a `fields_synced` out-parameter (same shape as the existing
   `subop_applied` out-parameter it already carries), filtered to the mirrored baseline fields.
3. `apply_handlers.handle_update` records that dict onto `BatchApplyContext.synced_fields`
   (the dataclass is defined in `apply_handlers.py:66`, not in `apply_base.py`)
   keyed by `local_id`. The 404 / assignee soft-fail arms return before the record, and the
   `record_backstop_failure` backstop never reaches it, so a soft-failed mutation contributes
   nothing.
4. `applier.apply` / `_apply_batch` accept a `synced_fields_out` dict out-parameter and copy
   `ctx.synced_fields` into it; `reconcile._apply_mutations` (reconcile.py:365, which calls
   `applier.apply` at lines 448/452) passes one in and stores it on the `_PassContext` for
   `_persist_and_log` -> `_advance_baselines` to consume.
5. `reconcile._advance_baselines` takes the synced map and, after `set_baseline` writes the
   pass-start snapshot, overlays the synced fields via a new
   `peer_state.merge_baseline` (a field-level overlay onto the existing baseline, as opposed to
   `set_baseline`'s whole-dict replace). The overlay also runs for a confirmed binding whose
   key was outside the fetch window, since our own push is fresh evidence even when the fetch
   was not.
6. **Observability for the deliberate non-advance.** A soft-failed mutation withholds its
   baseline advance silently today. `_advance_baselines` emits a single `RECON:
   baseline_overlay advanced=<n> fields=<n>` line to stderr per pass, and `handle_update`'s
   soft-fail arms already file a `bridge_alerts` entry — so an operator can tell "the baseline
   did not move because the push failed" from "the baseline did not move because there was
   nothing to push" without reading the manifest.

The mutation `fields` dict is already vendor-shaped at this point (post
`OutboundFieldMapper.map_fields_to_remote`: local `title` -> `summary`, status/priority ->
their Jira names, description ADF-fitted+normalized), which is exactly the shape
`peer_state.set_baseline` / `normalize_baseline_value` consume for `summary`, `description`,
`status` and `priority` — those four need no new mapping layer.

**`assignee` is the one field where that is NOT true, and it is handled deliberately rather than
assumed away.** A snapshot's `assignee` is a Jira user OBJECT, which the inbound mapper
canonicalizes into a display scalar plus an `assignee_identity` triple; the outbound mutation
carries only the single RESOLVED value (a bare display/email string, or an accountId when the
264f fast path set `_assignee_is_account_id`). So:

* Bare string (no fast path): the pushed value IS the local assignee string, so it is overlaid
  directly and the `_assignee_matches` guard resolves it exactly like a fetched scalar.
* accountId (fast path): the overlay records `{"accountId": <value>}`. The canonicalized
  baseline then carries that accountId as its only identity, which will NOT match a local
  assignee held as an email/display name — so the guard does not suppress and the pass falls
  back to today's local-wins push. That is the SAFE direction (a baseline that lags can only
  cause a redundant outbound re-push; a baseline that leads is the silent divergence the
  operator decision forbids), and it is chosen over fabricating a displayName/email we never
  observed. The residual ABA exposure for accountId-resolved assignees is pinned by an explicit
  test so it is a recorded limitation, not an accident.

**Also in scope — close the coverage gap.** ADR 0026 mandates a direction-preservation
regression cell and it exists for `title` only; the status equivalent
(`test_inbound_field_sync_directionality.py::test_jira_side_status_change_suppressed`) drives
`adapters/jira/outbound_fields._diff_fields`, which has **no production caller**. New cells are
added on the LIVE `outbound_field_diff.diff_canonical_fields` path for every mirrored field,
and the tests assert they executed the production path (an import-site assertion that the
function under test is the one `compute_update_fields` calls) so they cannot degrade into the
599e / 24f7 "passing by not running" class.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_one.py` — `_update_one_scalar_update` returns a
  per-call applied-fields dict; `update_one` gains the `fields_synced` out-parameter.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_handlers.py` — the `BatchApplyContext` dataclass
  (defined here at line 66) gains a `synced_fields` accumulator, and `handle_update` records
  into it on per-mutation success only.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/applier.py` — `apply` / `_apply_batch` `synced_fields_out`
  out-parameter.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile.py` — `_apply_mutations` collects the synced
  map onto `_PassContext`; `_persist_and_log` hands it to `_advance_baselines`, which overlays
  it after `set_baseline`.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/peer_state.py` — new `merge_baseline` field-level overlay.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_store.py` — thin `merge_baseline` delegate,
  matching the existing `set_baseline` delegate.
- `docs/adr/0026-reconciler-three-way-merge-baseline.md` — record that the baseline advance is
  last-synced (fetch overlaid with confirmed pushes), gated on per-mutation success.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` — new ABA-oracle, held-firm, soft-fail, and live-path
  direction-preservation cells (files named in Testing below).

**Module-size cap.** `dispatch_one.py` is at 785/800 LOC and `binding_store.py` at 782/800, so
the cap is a real constraint here. The `dispatch_one` change is written as an out-parameter on
`_update_one_scalar_update` (which `update_one` already calls) rather than a returned tuple,
keeping the delta to roughly ten lines. If it still crosses 800, the fallback is to extract the
existing sub-op dispatch cluster — `_update_one_dispatch_labels` / `_update_one_dispatch_links`
/ `_update_one_dispatch_comments` (lines 662-785, ~124 LOC, called only from `update_one`) —
into a new `dispatch_subops.py`. That is a pre-existing call-graph seam and clears >100 LOC, so
it satisfies the split policy; it is NOT a mechanical line-count carve. New baseline logic goes
in `peer_state.py` (the existing baseline home), never in `reconcile.py`.

## Testing

Assume the reconciler unit-test fakes (in-memory binding store + stub transport) are the
harness; no live Jira.

- **ABA oracle (RED first)** — `test_baseline_advance_aba.py`: baseline `To Do`; local pushed to
  `closed` and the push succeeds; local reverted to `open` before the next pass; assert pass N+1
  emits `status` outbound and the inbound differ does NOT clobber. Run against unmodified `main`
  first and record the failure, then fix.
- **Held-firm** — a genuine Jira-side status edit with local unchanged since the (correctly
  advanced) baseline still suppresses outbound and flows inbound. This is the guard against the
  fix silently becoming the rejected option B.
- **Soft-fail** — a status transition that raises `RuntimeError` from
  `transition_issue_by_name` (the `applier.py` backstop path) and a 400 illegal-transition
  comment-fallback: assert the baseline is NOT advanced for the failed field, and that a
  same-mutation field applied by a *separate* successful call is likewise not recorded
  (conservative all-or-nothing per `update_issue` call).
- **All five fields** — the ABA oracle and the direction-preservation cell are parameterized
  over `summary`/`description`/`priority`/`status`/`assignee`. The assignee cell asserts BOTH
  halves of the caveat above: a bare-string assignee push DOES close the ABA hole, and an
  accountId-resolved push falls back to local-wins (asserted explicitly, so the limitation is
  pinned rather than silently regressed).
- **Live-path direction preservation** — cells driving
  `outbound_field_diff.diff_canonical_fields` (the function `compute_update_fields` actually
  calls), asserting for each mirrored field that `local == baseline` + differing remote
  suppresses the outbound emit. Each cell asserts the production reachability of the function it
  drives, so it cannot pass by not running.
- **Empty/edge** — no synced fields (a pass with zero outbound updates) leaves
  `_advance_baselines` byte-identical to today; an unbound/unconfirmed `local_id` in the synced
  map is a no-op; an out-of-window key still receives its overlay.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The baseline for a field is advanced to the value rebar itself just pushed outbound, so
      `local == baseline` no longer means "local unchanged" for one pass after our own write
      (or an equivalent fix that removes the false premise)
- [ ] A test reproduces the ABA sequence end to end - baseline B, local pushed to A, local
      reverted to B before the next pass - and proves the status is NOT clobbered
- [ ] A test pins that the deliberate ADR 0026 behaviour is NOT weakened: a genuine Jira-side
      status edit against an unchanged local status still flows inbound
- [ ] The fix is applied to every inbound-mirrored field, or its restriction to status is stated
      with a reason (`_INBOUND_MIRRORED_FIELDS` = title, description, priority, status, assignee -
      all share the guard, so all share the ABA exposure)
